questions.question: When it is hard to see at dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, how can you let other drivers know you are there?
questions.explanation: Use your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly or when other drivers may not see you. Use your low beam headlights if you need to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: What should you do if bad weather makes it hard to see?

options.text: Speed up to leave the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: When visibility is poor, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. This gives you more time to stop or react if something unexpected happens.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a road with no curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the road edge.
Turn your wheels away from the road edge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the road edge.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the right (toward the road edge). If your brakes fail, the car will roll safely off the road.

questions.question: In Nebraska, what is the blood alcohol concentration (BAC) limit for drivers under 21?
questions.explanation: In Nebraska, drivers under 21 cannot operate a vehicle with a BAC of 0.02 percent or higher.

questions.question: On the interstate, where should slower traffic drive?
questions.explanation: On interstate highways, slower traffic must stay in the right lane. The left lane is for faster vehicles to pass.

questions.question: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers and must follow all traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Under Nebraska law, bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers and must obey all traffic laws. Motor vehicle drivers must respect bicyclists' right to use the road.

questions.question: When is it most dangerous to turn or stop in rainy weather?

options.text: After it has rained all day.
One half hour after the rain stops.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars mixes with rainwater on the road, creating a slippery surface.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down when turning to stay in control, keep your car in its lane, and react to unexpected situations.

questions.question: Speeding fines in work zones are:
questions.explanation: Speeding fines are doubled in work zones where workers are present and in school zones during school hours. Always drive carefully near workers and pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a divided highway is beginning ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a low ground railroad crossing. Railroad tracks cross the road at a steep slope. The bottom of low vehicles may drag or catch on the tracks.

questions.question: A bicyclist who breaks traffic laws:

options.text: Is correct because bicyclists do not have to follow traffic laws.
Will always get a warning from police.
Will have their bicycle taken away.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and duties as drivers. Both can be ticketed if they break traffic laws.

questions.question: Strong wind gusts on highways:

options.text: Can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: While strong wind can be harder on large vehicles, it affects all drivers. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dirt and dust on the road. It can also push any vehicle sideways.

questions.question: When a driver is tailgating you:

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If there is no right lane, slowly reduce your speed when the road ahead is clear. This lets the tailgater pass you.

questions.explanation: If you are tailgated and a right lane is open, move to it. If not, wait for clear road ahead and slowly reduce speed. This encourages the tailgater to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, look for other traffic, and drive carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign warns of a curve in the road.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic going both ways, you should:

options.text: Return to your lane when you have enough space between you and the passed vehicle.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right lane immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to your lane when you have enough space between you and the passed vehicle.
questions.explanation: After passing on a two-lane road, return to the right lane when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: How can you avoid rear-end collisions?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal and let your vehicle slow before braking.

questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. Release the gas to slow down first, then apply steady brake pressure. This activates your brake lights and stops your vehicle smoothly.

questions.question: When driving in rain, you must:
questions.explanation: In rain, use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: A driver turning left at an intersection must yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming bicycles just as you would to oncoming cars. Keep your wheels straight while waiting. Turn only when the way is clear of traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle, you must leave a note. Include your name, phone number, and address. Attach it securely to the vehicle you hit.

questions.question: When driving on slippery surfaces like snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Stay close behind other vehicles to keep traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Shift to a low gear before going down a steep hill on slippery surfaces. Follow other vehicles at a greater distance than normal. Avoid quick stops. If you do not have antilock brakes, pump the brakes gently to slow down.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel tightly and slow down gradually.
Turn on emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tightly and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes right away. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slow down by releasing the accelerator. When moving very slowly, apply the brakes gently and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the road edge, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until it is safe, then gradually return to the road.
Turn back onto the road immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until it is safe, then gradually return to the road.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back onto the road right away. Slow down, check traffic, and gradually turn back when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving near a large truck, what should you do?

options.text: Follow closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Do not drive beside it for long periods of time.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside it for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots on each side. Avoid driving beside them for long periods of time.
